pure-announcement.rationale: An argumentative essay on model supply-chain risk from Semgrep's blog, with no product being launched or funded.

duplicate.rationale: Nothing among the nearest concepts (RAG, SIEM gap, eval envelopes, weak-to-strong generalization) touches model provenance or backdoor detectability.

unfalsifiable.rationale: Its central claims are pinned to named sources — the sleeper-agent and poisoning papers, Anthropic's small-samples result, and Thompson's Turing lecture.

durability.rationale: The core asymmetry — binaries can be reverse-engineered but model weights cannot, while poisoning sample counts do not grow with model size — is a mechanism-level claim that will hold well beyond twelve months.

actionability.rationale: It prescribes an industry direction (provenance, reproducibility, independent audit over benchmarks) but gives an individual team no concrete practice to adopt today.

atomicity.rationale: Every section serves one statable idea: Thompson's trusting-trust problem applied to model lineage — trust must come from build-pipeline provenance because the artifact itself is uninspectable.
